# Plan for plaintiff's metallurgist (fatigue from design)

## What we do first

1. **Report to Evander Thorsby, and only him.** All case communications go through the General Counsel. I would send him a short written note with the expert's opinion, our preliminary read, and the steps below. We do not contact Joad engineers or production staff directly.
2. **Confirm the litigation hold is in place** for the component, design files, test data, and supplier records. Confirm whether the component is a JX-series spindle. If it is, or if we learn of other JX-series incidents, we report them to him immediately.
3. **Get a protective order in place before any internal test data goes out.** Joad's instruction is no stipulation to authenticity or business-record admissibility of its test data until then. After that we address authenticity document by document, with no blanket stipulation. Until then, the circle of people who see test files stays tight.
4. **Ask Thorsby to arrange early interviews of the key engineers**, such as the chief axle engineer. Joad wants to discuss with us before any employee is put forward as a witness, so the interviews are for fact-gathering, and witness designation comes later.

## The plan for the expert

- **Retain our own experts, subject to client clearance.** We need a fatigue and metallurgy expert and a design expert. We send Joad names, credentials, and prior-testimony notes, ideally several candidates per discipline, before anyone is engaged. We build that clearance time into the timeline.
- **Tell Joad whether anyone will address industry practice.** Joad prefers design testimony to stay focused on the product at issue. It has offered to help identify candidates who have served on standards bodies, and we should take it up on that.
- **Test the opinion in three ways.**
  - First, whether the fracture surface evidence actually supports a design-driven fatigue origin.
  - Second, whether the cause could be material, forging, or manufacturing, or service conditions such as overload or misuse. Any alternative-cause theory must be handled with care (see the caution below).
  - Third, whether the plaintiff's methodology and the testing behind it hold up to a reliability challenge.
- **Testing.** We get quotes first and give Joad ten days' notice of any proposed testing. We also settle who pays for shared lab work. Expert and testing costs will drive most of the budget variance.

## Cautions specific to Joad

- **Supplier change and Corbelmark.** Joad changed its spindle forging supplier in 2020 after an internal audit, and it asked that the reason stay within the case team. If we pursue a material or forging theory, or the plaintiff's expert probes supplier issues, this becomes sensitive. We learn Corbelmark before any supplier discussion. We do not share the reason for the change with our outside experts or anyone else without Thorsby's approval.
- **No public statements.** Media, regulator, and customer inquiries go to Thorsby.

## Reporting, budget, insurance, and settlement

- **Case assessment.** Our first assessment is due within 60 days. It will include an exposure range and a probability of an adverse result, and the plaintiff's expert theory feeds directly into it.
- **Budget.** We provide a phase budget that covers expert and testing costs.
- **Six-week reports.** Written reports go out every six weeks, with a call after significant events. Any deposition of the plaintiff's metallurgist gets a short note within five business days, and attendance is limited to one firm lawyer and one insurer lawyer.
- **Insurer.** We copy Perpetua Wallace (Cobaltridge Indemnity) on anything bearing on coverage or exposure and send her the monthly invoice summary. The retention was $400,000, and Joad watches the aggregate limit because of other open claims. It wants same-day notice if the carrier reserves rights.
- **Settlement authority.** The $1.5M insurer pre-approval comes from an earlier matter, so I would ask Thorsby to confirm it in writing for C-2. If exposure could exceed that tier, we flag the roughly three-week board consent process now. No number above the insurer tier is communicated, even as a signal, without written board sign-off. Even for an offer within the insurer tier, we consult Joad first because the insurer will want to be involved.
